newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan body mulls seeking jusen borrower bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Japan body mulls seeking jusen borrower bankruptcy.

text.p: The Housing Loan Administration Corp (HLAC), set up to collect problem loans run up by Japan's failed "jusen" mortgage firms, is considering asking a court to declare realtor Sueno Kosan, a major borrower from the firms, bankrupt, the HLAC president said on Friday.
Kohei Nakabo, president of the corporation, told reporters that the timing of any such request had not yet been decided.
Japanese media reported earlier this week that the corporation was considering the action because of the realtor's attempt to hide assets by transferring them to affiliates.
In September, Sueno Kosan chief Kenichi Sueno pleaded guilty in the Osaka District Court to charges that he and some aides hid assets to prevent them being seized by creditors.
Japanese media said total liabilities at the Osaka-based firm were estimated at 560 billion yen on a parent company basis and at 670 billion yen on a group basis.

The group was the second-largest borrower from the mortgage firms. It borrowed 236.7 billion yen from five of the seven jusen and about 300 billion yen from 10 other financial institutions, they said.
Sueno Kosan is not a listed company. If it is declared bankrupt, it would be one of the biggest Japanese insolvencies in history, financial industry sources said.
They said that if the firm goes under, creditor non-bank financial institutions were likely to face business difficulties.
Nakabo said such concerns would not affect HLAC's decision.
